clue.text: Prepare to discharge mine in scene of conflict

parts.note: to cock a gun is to make it ready to fire
a coal mine is a pit

explanation.surface: Someone readies explosives at a mine on a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit was an arena for cock fights, so by extension any place where battles are fought.

clue.text: Method of payment providing firm's first capital

parts.note: providing means on condition that, if

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter alone of the word before it

explanation.surface: A company is asked about payment methods to raise start-up capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, tying in with payment and firm; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Make more vulgar, getting a censor agitated

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer cheapens the content, upsetting a censor.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen is to make rougher or cruder, so less refined and more vulgar.

clue.text: Said group of wild animals had a curious look

indicators.note: said points to how the following words sound when spoken, not how they are written

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions

explanation.surface: A pack of wild beasts peered inquisitively at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pry is to look or inquire nosily, and pried is its past tense.

clue.text: Asian philosopher has little time to put in as superficial decorator

indicators.note: has means holds within, so the philosopher contains the words put in

parts.note: a Taoist follows the Chinese philosophy of Tao
T is the abbreviation for time
to is taken as written; put in signals it goes inside

explanation.surface: A busy Eastern sage has little time for shallow decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: A Taoist follows the Chinese philosophy of Tao. 'Superficial' sounds like a sneer; here it means on the surface of the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist decorates people's skin, literally on the surface, hence superficial.

clue.text: Got to grips with change — of course, provided with guidance

parts.note: in sailing, to tack is to change course

explanation.surface: Someone dealt with a change of plan, naturally after being guided.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'of course' look like 'naturally'; it actually completes the sailing phrase change of course.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to engage with it in earnest, the same idiom as getting to grips.

clue.text: Understood how attic might be reconstructed

indicators.note: reconstruction rebuilds something in a new form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder grasps how the loft could be redone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied rather than stated, so it is understood without words.

clue.text: Artist carefully studies figures systematically arranged

parts.note: to con is to study or learn carefully
a table sets out numbers in ordered rows and columns

explanation.surface: A painter carefully studies figures arranged in his composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Systematically arranged' looks like an anagram signal, but it describes a table of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Apprentice left lucrative job

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a nice earner is a job that pays well

explanation.surface: A trainee quit a well-paid position.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is someone still learning a trade, hence a beginner or trainee.

clue.text: Sped off with painting as plunder

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: Thieves raced away with a canvas as loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to strip of valuables, the verb sense of plundering.

clue.text: One who's pragmatic about a problem for vessel

parts.note: a ship in trouble lists, leaning to one side

explanation.surface: A practical person deals with some difficulty affecting a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist accepts things as they are and acts practically, a synonym for a pragmatic person.

clue.text: Sails south in attempt to raise political support

parts.note: sails are made of canvas, which stands for them
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A yacht heads south in some campaign to win votes.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to go door to door seeking votes, an attempt to win backing for a party.

clue.text: At home and away, covering team very thoroughly

indicators.note: the two words on either side wrap around and enclose what follows

explanation.surface: A reporter covers a football team's home and away matches in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and OUT go either side of SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is an idiom for knowing it completely and in every detail.

clue.text: Dance music is what ends concert heard on radio

indicators.note: radio operators speak letters as codewords, so the kept letter is swapped for its spoken code name
what ends a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: A listener notes which dance tune closes a concert broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used on radio, T is spoken as Tango.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a Latin American dance, and the word also names the music written for it.

clue.text: Closing section of shelf in a library

indicators.note: a section is only a part, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across shelf, in, a and library

explanation.surface: Someone describes the last section of shelving in a library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closing section' reads as one phrase, but Closing alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Final and closing are synonyms, both meaning coming at the end.

clue.text: City in which man's name is heard — he's seen when ice disappears

indicators.note: is heard means the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: a second, confirming route: take ice out of the city's spelling and the man's name is left

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a city where a man's name rings out, and who appears when ice melts.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is pronounced like Lester, a quirk of English place names; the dash adds a confirmation, since removing ICE from the city's spelling leaves LESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Mean one-line defamatory text about artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
a libel is a written defamation
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A spiteful one-liner libels a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb or average, but here it is the adjective for ungenerous or narrow-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal can mean ungenerous or stingy, the sense of mean as tight with money or narrow-minded.

clue.text: Secure Labour leader in faction gets decisive electoral result

parts.note: to land a deal is to secure it

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a leader is at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A party chief who holds the factions together wins big at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' looks like a politician, but it is just the first letter of Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an overwhelming election victory, by metaphor with a mass of earth sweeping all before it.

clue.text: Another sport in place of equestrian events

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a racket game played with a shuttlecock
second meaning: the Gloucestershire estate that hosts famous horse trials

explanation.surface: A different sport is played where the horse events usually take place.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton House in Gloucestershire, England, hosts the annual Badminton Horse Trials; the racket game is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The shuttlecock game took its name from the ducal estate where horse trials are now held.

clue.text: Lying in sun, very hot without shade, initially

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece goes around the other
initially keeps only the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A sunbather lies out in fierce heat with no shade to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bask is to lie warming yourself, as a lizard does in sunshine.

clue.text: Wrong done with gun in prison cell

indicators.note: wrong means not as it should be, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A crime committed with a firearm ends with a spell behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell in a castle where prisoners were kept.

clue.text: Animal's lair or home for humans

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fox's or badger's burrow

explanation.surface: A contrast between where a wild creature lives and where people live.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox goes to earth in its burrow, and the planet we inhabit carries the same name.

clue.text: Way to restore order once in port, supported by diplomacy

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A port is kept calm by diplomacy once trouble breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, supported by puts the second piece below the first. 'Once in port' reads together, but once belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act, an old British law, was read aloud to disperse unruly crowds, a historical means of keeping the peace.

clue.text: Firm about a sort of Bible university in America

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A company deals with a particular edition of scripture for an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: The Revised Version is an 1880s English revision of the King James Bible, abbreviated in two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard is the Ivy League university in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

clue.text: For example, taste part of chosen selection

indicators.note: only a part is wanted, so the letters are found within the following words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of chosen and start of selection

explanation.surface: A wine taster samples part of a chosen selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, so it is given as an example of the category.

clue.text: Place for holding water as river rose disastrously

indicators.note: a disaster throws things into chaos, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A flood warning: a dam was needed because the river rose disastrously.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake that stores water for supply.

clue.text: Turn up unlike clergy or VIP

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: lay people are those not ordained

explanation.surface: Someone tells a layman or an important guest to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: A royal is a member of a royal family, used here loosely as a noun for a very important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal, a member of a monarch's family, is the archetypal very important person.

clue.text: Right above a diameter, two other lines in circle

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
D is the symbol for diameter

explanation.surface: Geometry: one line is drawn above a diameter, and two more inside a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, above puts R before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are straight segments from the centre of a circle to its edge, each half a diameter.

clue.text: I destroyed plenty with clumsy actions

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so these letters are rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A confession from someone who broke lots of things through carelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptly means awkwardly or without skill, which describes clumsy behaviour.

clue.text: Land in East and North, a part of US

parts.note: India is a country in the East
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone tours lands to the east and north, then a region of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land in East' looks like a container instruction, but it simply describes India.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the US, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Haphazard gleaner is not particular

indicators.note: haphazard means random and disorderly, so the letters fall in a random order

explanation.surface: A field worker collecting leftover grain is careless about what is picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: General means broad rather than specific, the opposite of particular.

clue.text: Was left embracing son

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent departed while hugging their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was left' reads as a passive verb, but Was alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Was and existed both mean had being, the past of the verb to be in its sense of to exist.
